title: Mutable argument default leaks state across calls
aliases: trạng thái chia sẻ alias tham chiếu mutable thay đổi dữ liệu

where.summary: Function parameters with list, dict, set or another mutable default.
preconditions: The function mutates a default object and callers expect independent calls.
where.location_template: At {location} in {target}, inspect: Function parameters with list, dict, set or another mutable default.

how.mechanism: A default object is created at function definition and reused when the argument is omitted.

what.observable_failure: The second call contains state left by the first call.
what.oracle_template: Under {contract}, compare the second result and side effects with a call using a fresh explicit default.

applicability_notes: Shared defaults can be an intentional cache; establish the independence contract first.

title: Definition-time call freezes a supposedly fresh value

what.observable_failure: Later invocations use an old timestamp, token or object.
what.oracle_template: Under {contract}, check that each invocation observes the required current state or a distinct object.

applicability_notes: Immutable constants and deliberately captured snapshots are valid uses.

what.observable_failure: The second instance observes changes intended only for the first.
what.oracle_template: Under {contract}, assert that instance-specific state of the second instance stays unchanged.

applicability_notes: ClassVar registries and explicitly shared caches intentionally share state.

title: A broad exception assertion accepts the wrong failure

what.observable_failure: The test passes without establishing the intended behavior.
what.oracle_template: Under {exception_contract}, assert the required exception class, message or attributes and the exact raising operation.

title: An exception assertion can pass on an earlier unintended statement

what.oracle_template: Under {exception_contract}, separate setup from the assertion context and assert the exception at the intended call.

applicability_notes: Several statements can be intentional, but the raising site must still match the test claim.

title: Assertions used for runtime validation vanish in optimized mode

title: A saved dictionary view changes with the dictionary

what.observable_failure: A supposed snapshot contains added or changed entries, or iteration fails after a size change.

applicability_notes: Live views are intentional and efficient; mutation of an existing value differs from changing dictionary size.

title: A default argument expression runs even when its value is unused
aliases: điều kiện logic so sánh boolean sai kết quả

applicability_notes: Eager evaluation is Python semantics and may be intended; this is an application assumption to verify.

title: Prefix increment or decrement does not update a Python number

what.observable_failure: The counter stays unchanged and loop progress or counts are wrong.

title: Attribute presence is mistaken for callability

title: A standalone comparison fails to enforce an intended condition

where.location_template: At {location} in {target}, inspect: A comparison appears as an expression statement with its result unused.

what.observable_failure: Execution continues without the expected rejection or update.
what.oracle_template: Under {contract}, assert the required rejection or state transition independently of evaluating the comparison.

applicability_notes: Overloaded comparisons can have side effects; inspect operand types before treating the statement as inert.

title: An f-string in docstring position leaves __doc__ unset

where.location_template: At {location} in {target}, inspect: The first statement of a function, class or module is an f-string.

what.observable_failure: The expected documentation is absent from __doc__ or automated tooling.

title: Missing abstract decorators permit an incomplete implementation

where.location_template: At {location} in {target}, inspect: An ABC or an empty interface method lacks the intended abstractmethod decorator.

what.observable_failure: An incomplete object is accepted and may run an empty stub instead of required behavior.
what.oracle_template: Under {interface_contract}, assert abstract status and rejection of incomplete implementations.

applicability_notes: ABCs can intentionally provide concrete mixin methods; absence of a decorator alone does not prove a bug.

title: Explicit and unpacked call arguments bind the same parameter

what.observable_failure: Argument binding raises TypeError; repeated explicit keyword syntax can instead fail compilation.
what.oracle_template: Under {call_contract}, assert successful unique binding or the required explicit collision rejection.

applicability_notes: A star argument after a keyword is legal when bindings do not overlap; do not reject the syntax categorically.

title: Warning location points to the wrapper instead of the caller

what.observable_failure: The warning filename or line identifies the library internals rather than the relevant caller.
what.oracle_template: Under {warning_contract}, assert captured warning filename, line and category at the intended origin.

applicability_notes: A wrapper may intentionally report its own location; skip_file_prefixes availability depends on Python version.

title: A set collapses repeated values that the application needed to retain

where.summary: A set literal includes duplicate values or is used as though it preserves input multiplicity.
preconditions: The application requires distinct entries, counts or a missing distinct literal was intended.
where.location_template: At {location} in {target}, inspect: A set literal includes duplicate values or is used as though it preserves input multiplicity.

what.observable_failure: Required cardinality or multiplicity is lost, or a copy-paste typo hides a missing distinct entry.
what.oracle_template: Under {collection_contract}, check the expected distinct members and whether multiplicity must be preserved.

title: Custom exception initialization breaks copying or pickling

where.location_template: At {location} in {target}, inspect: An exception subclass defines a custom __init__ whose argument state is incompatible with reconstruction.

how.trigger_template: Create {exception_instance} with {constructor_arguments}; round-trip it through the required copy or serialization operation.

what.observable_failure: Reconstruction raises or loses required exception state or message.
what.oracle_template: Under {exception_contract}, assert type, required attributes, args and message after the round-trip.

applicability_notes: Custom __reduce__ or __str__ can legitimately supply alternative protocols; untrusted pickle data must never be loaded.

title: Exception translation loses the intended explicit cause

where.summary: An except block raises a replacement exception without explicit chaining policy.
preconditions: The error API specifies a cause or deliberate suppression of underlying context.
where.location_template: At {location} in {target}, inspect: An except block raises a replacement exception without explicit chaining policy.

how.mechanism: Implicit context differs from an explicit __cause__ and from raise ... from None suppression.

what.observable_failure: The exception cause, context display or diagnostic chain differs from the error contract.
what.oracle_template: Under {error_contract}, inspect __cause__, __context__ and __suppress_context__ as appropriate.

applicability_notes: Implicit chaining preserves context automatically; lack of from does not itself mean all cause information is lost.

title: An AST visitor override silently skips child nodes

where.location_template: At {location} in {target}, inspect: A NodeVisitor visit_* override does not visit relevant child nodes.

what.observable_failure: Nested findings or transformations are missing.
what.oracle_template: Under {traversal_contract}, assert the required visited node set and nested findings.

applicability_notes: Some visitors intentionally prune subtrees; verify traversal policy before adding generic_visit.

title: Manually quoting a value fails to escape embedded quotes or control characters

what.observable_failure: The output is ambiguous or spans unintended lines.
what.oracle_template: Under {representation_contract}, compare with the required escaped representation for the supported value type.

title: Reading a missing defaultdict key unexpectedly changes the mapping

what.observable_failure: The mapping grows or later iteration includes keys that were only probed.

title: Extra formatting arguments hide an omitted output field

what.observable_failure: The required field is absent and changing its value does not affect output.

title: Invalid starred assignment prevents compilation

what.observable_failure: Compilation raises SyntaxError before the module can run.
what.oracle_template: Under {language_contract}, assert that required source compiles or invalid source is rejected at the specified stage.

title: A misplaced or unsupported __future__ import prevents compilation

where.summary: A future import follows executable statements or requests an unsupported feature.
preconditions: Compilation occurs on the target Python version.
where.location_template: At {location} in {target}, inspect: A future import follows executable statements or requests an unsupported feature.

what.observable_failure: The module fails with SyntaxError before import-time code executes.
what.oracle_template: Under {compatibility_contract}, assert successful compilation for every supported interpreter version.

applicability_notes: A module docstring and permitted leading statements have special placement rules; feature support varies by version.

title: A wildcard import in a non-module scope is rejected

what.oracle_template: Under {language_contract}, assert valid import placement or the required SyntaxError for invalid input.

title: Python 2 print redirection is interpreted as an unsupported operator in Python 3

what.observable_failure: Execution fails or no required text reaches the intended stream.
what.oracle_template: Under {output_contract}, assert the exact bytes or text written to the required stream.

title: A control-flow statement is illegal in its enclosing scope or Python version

what.oracle_template: Under {language_contract}, assert compilation and diagnostics appropriate to the supported scope and version.

title: A bare except before another handler makes the try statement invalid

what.oracle_template: Under {language_contract}, assert valid handler ordering or the required rejection for invalid source.

title: Rebinding a parameter, receiver or assignment target destroys a still-needed value

what.oracle_template: Under {binding_contract}, assert the expected original or replacement value at each required use.

what.oracle_template: Under {typing_contract}, assert the permitted variance definition and its diagnostic or construction behavior.

title: Duplicate base or Generic inheritance rejects a class definition

title: A bare raise executes without an active exception

how.mechanism: Bidirectional display reordering can make comments, strings or neighboring source appear in a misleading order.
how.trigger_template: Inspect {source_fragment} in escaped-codepoint form and compare its tokens or AST with the displayed rendering.

what.observable_failure: A reviewer or source consumer attributes behavior to the wrong apparent code region.
what.oracle_template: Under {source_contract}, compare parsed behavior with the intended logic and enforce the required source-display policy.

applicability_notes: Legitimate right-to-left text is common; presence of a control character does not by itself prove a vulnerability.

title: A property getter requires arguments that attribute access cannot supply

where.summary: A property getter requires positional or keyword arguments beyond its receiver.
preconditions: The property is read through normal attribute access.
where.location_template: At {location} in {target}, inspect: A property getter requires positional or keyword arguments beyond its receiver.

how.mechanism: The descriptor calls its getter with the instance and does not receive application-supplied method arguments.
how.trigger_template: Construct {instance} and read {property_name} through attribute access.

what.observable_failure: The getter raises a missing-argument TypeError.
what.oracle_template: Under {property_contract}, assert attribute access returns the required value without extra call arguments.

applicability_notes: Optional getter parameters can be satisfied by defaults; a method intended to take arguments may be a better API.

title: A loop else executes after a successful search because no break occurs

where.summary: A search loop has an else clause but no relevant break.
preconditions: The else branch is intended only for a failed search.
where.location_template: At {location} in {target}, inspect: A search loop has an else clause but no relevant break.

how.mechanism: Loop else runs on normal exhaustion regardless of whether a match was encountered unless the loop exits with break.
how.trigger_template: Supply {items} containing a match for {predicate} and then allow normal exhaustion.

what.observable_failure: The not-found branch runs after successful processing.
what.oracle_template: Under {search_contract}, assert found and not-found effects are mutually correct for matching, missing and empty inputs.

applicability_notes: A loop else can intentionally run on normal exhaustion; return and exceptions also affect control flow.

title: A mistaken self-assignment leaves required state unchanged

where.summary: A variable is assigned to itself where an update or different source value was intended.
preconditions: The required state transition changes that binding.
where.location_template: At {location} in {target}, inspect: A variable is assigned to itself where an update or different source value was intended.

how.mechanism: Ordinary name self-assignment stores the same object reference without performing the intended computation.
how.trigger_template: Execute {assignment_site} with distinct {current_value} and {required_value}.

what.observable_failure: The stored value stays unchanged.
what.oracle_template: Under {state_contract}, assert the required post-assignment value and downstream effect.

applicability_notes: Attribute assignment can invoke descriptors and is not necessarily inert; this card concerns ordinary name bindings.

title: An invalid file mode rejects opening before the intended I/O

where.summary: open receives an invalid mode character or incompatible combination of modes.
preconditions: The target interpreter and file API enforce that mode grammar.
where.location_template: At {location} in {target}, inspect: open receives an invalid mode character or incompatible combination of modes.

how.mechanism: File-opening mode parsing rejects unsupported or contradictory flags.
how.trigger_template: Call {open_expression} with a temporary file and the exact {mode_value} on {target_interpreter}.

what.observable_failure: Opening raises before the required read, write or create operation.
what.oracle_template: Under {file_contract}, assert supported mode behavior and required invalid-mode rejection.

applicability_notes: Historical modes such as U have version-specific support; use the actual supported Python versions.

title: A shallow copy of os.environ still changes process environment state

where.summary: copy.copy is used on the os.environ proxy as though it produced an independent environment snapshot.
preconditions: The caller intends mutations of the copy not to affect process environment state.
where.location_template: At {location} in {target}, inspect: copy.copy is used on the os.environ proxy as though it produced an independent environment snapshot.

how.mechanism: The shallow proxy copy retains shared backing state and environment mutation behavior.
how.trigger_template: In an isolated process, shallow-copy os.environ and mutate a dedicated {test_key} through {copied_proxy}.

what.observable_failure: The original environment or child-process environment changes unexpectedly.
what.oracle_template: Under {environment_contract}, assert isolation of the original mapping and required child environment.

applicability_notes: os.environ.copy() or an explicit dict snapshot has different semantics; never test with existing secret-bearing keys.

title: preexec_fn can deadlock a child forked from a multithreaded process

where.summary: subprocess.Popen uses preexec_fn while the parent has multiple threads.
preconditions: The child callback can encounter a lock inherited from a thread absent in the child.
where.location_template: At {location} in {target}, inspect: subprocess.Popen uses preexec_fn while the parent has multiple threads.

how.mechanism: After fork, locks can remain held without their owning thread, blocking child setup before exec.
how.trigger_template: Review {preexec_callback} and reproduce {controlled_lock_schedule} only in a bounded isolated subprocess harness.

what.observable_failure: Child creation or pre-exec setup hangs before the intended command runs.
what.oracle_template: Under {process_contract}, assert bounded child startup and required process setup using documented subprocess options.

applicability_notes: Scheduling is nondeterministic; a passing run cannot prove safety, and every reproduction needs timeout and cleanup.

title: An assertion prints its message but stores None in the exception

where.summary: An assert message expression is print(message).
preconditions: Consumers require the diagnostic in AssertionError rather than only stdout.
where.location_template: At {location} in {target}, inspect: An assert message expression is print(message).

how.mechanism: print returns None, so the failing assertion stores None as its message after producing a stdout side effect.
how.trigger_template: Make {asserted_condition} false and capture both AssertionError.args and stdout.

what.observable_failure: The exception lacks the required message and output appears on an unexpected channel.
what.oracle_template: Under {diagnostic_contract}, assert the exception arguments and output channels independently.

applicability_notes: This changes diagnostics rather than whether the assertion condition fails; explicit print side effects can be intentional.

title: A __post_init__ default does not make an InitVar constructor argument optional

where.summary: A dataclass __post_init__ parameter has a default while its corresponding InitVar field does not.
preconditions: The generated constructor is expected to allow omitting that init-only argument.
where.location_template: At {location} in {target}, inspect: A dataclass __post_init__ parameter has a default while its corresponding InitVar field does not.

how.mechanism: The generated __init__ signature comes from dataclass field declarations, not defaults on __post_init__.
how.trigger_template: Instantiate {dataclass} while omitting {initvar_parameter}, then inspect the generated constructor signature.

what.observable_failure: Instantiation raises a missing-argument error despite the __post_init__ default.
what.oracle_template: Under {construction_contract}, assert the generated signature and required omitted-argument behavior.

applicability_notes: Defaults in __post_init__ can affect direct calls to it; they do not define generated constructor defaults.

title: Copied identical branches erase a required distinction between cases

where.summary: Conditional branches or if-expression arms contain identical outcomes.
preconditions: The specification requires at least two cases to produce different results or effects.
where.location_template: At {location} in {target}, inspect: Conditional branches or if-expression arms contain identical outcomes.

how.mechanism: Both branches perform the same computation despite the intended distinction.
how.trigger_template: Supply {first_case} and {second_case} that the contract requires to behave differently.

what.observable_failure: The required output or side-effect distinction is absent.
what.oracle_template: Under {branch_contract}, compare outcomes for each distinct specified case.

applicability_notes: Identical branches are often a valid simplification opportunity; only a differing contract establishes a bug.

title: An assertion message is mistaken for an expected comparison value

where.summary: An assertion uses a computed value as its condition and the expected literal as its message.
preconditions: The test intends exact equality rather than a truthiness test.
where.location_template: At {location} in {target}, inspect: An assertion uses a computed value as its condition and the expected literal as its message.

how.mechanism: assert actual, expected checks only actual truthiness and reserves expected for failure diagnostics.
how.trigger_template: Choose {actual_value} that is truthy but unequal to {expected_value}, then execute {assertion}.

what.observable_failure: The assertion passes despite a wrong value.
what.oracle_template: Under {value_contract}, assert the required equality or other comparison directly.

applicability_notes: Non-string assertion messages are legal; the failure requires evidence that an exact comparison was intended.

title: An unannotated dataclass attribute is not an instance constructor field

where.summary: A dataclass body assigns an unannotated attribute intended as a field.
preconditions: The caller expects that attribute to appear in generated __init__ or per-instance field metadata.
where.location_template: At {location} in {target}, inspect: A dataclass body assigns an unannotated attribute intended as a field.

how.mechanism: An unannotated assignment remains a class attribute instead of a dataclass field.
how.trigger_template: Construct {dataclass} with {attribute} as a keyword and inspect dataclass field metadata.

what.observable_failure: The constructor rejects the keyword or the required field is missing.
what.oracle_template: Under {field_contract}, assert the constructor signature, field list and intended per-instance state.

applicability_notes: Class constants are intentionally not fields; a mutable class attribute has an additional sharing risk covered separately.

title: Splitting a version into integers rejects legitimate release suffixes

where.summary: A version string is split on dots and every component is passed to int.
preconditions: Supported versions may include prerelease, postrelease, development or local suffixes.
where.location_template: At {location} in {target}, inspect: A version string is split on dots and every component is passed to int.

how.mechanism: A package version need not consist only of dot-separated integer components.
how.trigger_template: Parse {version_string} containing a supported nonnumeric suffix alongside a plain release control case.

what.observable_failure: Parsing raises ValueError or version handling rejects a supported release.
what.oracle_template: Under {version_contract}, assert acceptance and ordering for the exact supported version scheme.

applicability_notes: Use a parser for the required scheme; not every arbitrary application version claims packaging-version compliance.

title: Decorating an Enum as a dataclass collapses required member distinctions

where.summary: An Enum class is directly decorated with dataclass.
preconditions: Distinct enum members must compare as distinct in the application.
where.location_template: At {location} in {target}, inspect: An Enum class is directly decorated with dataclass.

how.mechanism: Dataclass-generated comparison behavior can interfere with normal enum member equality.
how.trigger_template: Define {enum_class} and compare two distinct {members} under {target_interpreter}.

what.observable_failure: Distinct members compare equal or other generated dataclass behavior violates the enum contract.
what.oracle_template: Under {enum_contract}, assert identity and required equality relationships for distinct members.

applicability_notes: An enum with a dataclass mixin is a different design; supported combinations and behavior vary by Python version.

title: A form-feed inside indentation changes or obscures block structure

where.summary: Leading whitespace contains a form-feed after a space or tab.
preconditions: The displayed indentation is assumed to match the intended parsed block structure.
where.location_template: At {location} in {target}, inspect: Leading whitespace contains a form-feed after a space or tab.

how.mechanism: Form-feed within indentation has interpreter-dependent or undefined indentation effects beyond the documented leading case.
how.trigger_template: Inspect escaped whitespace in {source_fragment} and parse or compile it with {target_interpreter}.

what.observable_failure: Compilation fails or the parsed block grouping differs from the required source structure.
what.oracle_template: Under {source_contract}, compare parsed nesting with intended nesting and enforce the chosen whitespace policy.

applicability_notes: Do not assume a portable exact indentation effect; a form-feed at the beginning of a line has separately documented handling.

title: Direct class-dictionary annotation access misses version-dependent annotations

where.summary: Annotation introspection reads cls.__dict__["__annotations__"] or .get directly.
preconditions: The code supports annotation storage or evaluation behavior not represented by that raw dictionary entry.
where.location_template: At {location} in {target}, inspect: Annotation introspection reads cls.__dict__["__annotations__"] or .get directly.

how.mechanism: The class dictionary is not a stable public abstraction for every supported Python annotation implementation.
how.trigger_template: Inspect {class_with_annotations} under each supported {annotation_mode} and Python version.

what.observable_failure: Required annotations are missing, a KeyError occurs or the consumer receives incomplete metadata.
what.oracle_template: Under {annotation_contract}, compare required annotation names and evaluation policy using the version-appropriate public introspection API.

applicability_notes: Deferred annotation APIs can evaluate expressions; preserve the specified evaluation policy and do not treat all introspection functions as identical.

title: A decimal permission literal sets different bits than intended octal permissions

where.summary: chmod or another mode-taking API receives a decimal-looking permission literal.
preconditions: The intended value was expressed as familiar octal permission digits.
where.location_template: At {location} in {target}, inspect: chmod or another mode-taking API receives a decimal-looking permission literal.

how.mechanism: The numeric literal is interpreted in its written radix, so decimal digits and octal digits represent different bitmasks.
how.trigger_template: Apply {mode_literal} to a temporary resource and inspect its permission bits on {target_platform}.

what.observable_failure: The resulting access bits differ from the intended permission policy.
what.oracle_template: Under {permission_contract}, compare the masked actual permissions with the required octal bitmask.

applicability_notes: A decimal bitmask may be intentional; umask and platform semantics must be accounted for separately.

title: A textual path prefix is mistaken for a common path component

where.summary: os.path.commonprefix is used for path ancestry or a shared-directory decision.
preconditions: The contract requires component boundaries or containment rather than character overlap.
where.location_template: At {location} in {target}, inspect: os.path.commonprefix is used for path ancestry or a shared-directory decision.

how.mechanism: commonprefix compares characters and can return a partial component shared by unrelated paths.
how.trigger_template: Use {paths} with a common spelling but different directory components, such as a directory name and a longer sibling name.

what.observable_failure: The computed ancestor is invalid or an unrelated sibling is classified as inside the required directory.
what.oracle_template: Under {path_contract}, assert component-aware ancestry under the required normalization and filesystem semantics.

applicability_notes: commonpath alone does not resolve symlinks or establish a complete filesystem containment policy; textual prefix is valid for purely textual tasks.

title: A receiver default allows an unintended unbound method call

where.summary: An instance receiver parameter has a default such as self=None.
preconditions: The method must operate on an explicitly bound instance and direct class calls should not silently use a fallback receiver.
where.location_template: At {location} in {target}, inspect: An instance receiver parameter has a default such as self=None.

how.mechanism: Calling an instance method through the class does not supply self; the parameter default can mask the missing receiver.
how.trigger_template: Invoke {method} through both {bound_instance} and its class without an explicit receiver.

what.observable_failure: The unbound call uses the fallback receiver or fails later with a misleading attribute error.
what.oracle_template: Under {method_contract}, assert required binding behavior and explicit rejection or documented handling of unbound calls.

applicability_notes: Ordinary bound classmethods already receive cls; a receiver default may be intentional for explicit class-level invocation.

title: Membership checks the container protocol rather than the intended application domain

where.summary: in or not in is used on mappings, strings or other containers with different membership semantics.
preconditions: The application expects value membership, exact tokens or another domain not supplied by that container protocol.
where.location_template: At {location} in {target}, inspect: in or not in is used on mappings, strings or other containers with different membership semantics.

how.mechanism: dict membership tests keys; string membership tests substrings, and an empty string is a substring of every string.
how.trigger_template: Use {container} where {candidate} is present only as a value, partial substring or empty string, rather than as an intended member.

what.observable_failure: The membership decision disagrees with the required domain.
what.oracle_template: Under {membership_contract}, assert membership over the explicit required key, value, token or substring domain.

applicability_notes: These are normal Python semantics; select the intended domain from the specification before judging the result.

title: Membership against an always-empty collection cannot distinguish candidates

where.summary: A membership condition uses a collection that is empty on every relevant path.
preconditions: The condition is intended to accept at least one candidate.
where.location_template: At {location} in {target}, inspect: A membership condition uses a collection that is empty on every relevant path.

how.mechanism: Membership in an empty built-in collection is false for every candidate; not in is true.
how.trigger_template: Evaluate {membership_condition} for both {accepted_candidate} and {rejected_candidate}.

what.observable_failure: A required acceptance or rejection branch cannot be reached.
what.oracle_template: Under {membership_contract}, assert different required outcomes and verify collection initialization.

applicability_notes: Constant membership tests can be intentional; custom __contains__ methods may not follow built-in empty-container semantics.

title: A subclass slot shadows distinct storage owned by its base class

where.summary: A subclass declares a slot with the same name as an inherited slot.
preconditions: Base-class and subclass behavior assume one consistent attribute storage location.
where.location_template: At {location} in {target}, inspect: A subclass declares a slot with the same name as an inherited slot.

how.mechanism: The subclass descriptor hides the base descriptor under ordinary attribute lookup, while the base slot can still be accessed through its own descriptor.
how.trigger_template: Create {instance}, store distinguishable values through {base_slot_descriptor} and ordinary {attribute} access, then run the affected base operation.

what.observable_failure: The base operation or serializer observes different storage from ordinary attribute access or cannot retrieve required state.
what.oracle_template: Under {attribute_contract}, assert consistent required state across normal access and the supported base-class operations.

applicability_notes: Slot redefinition is discouraged and behavior can be implementation-sensitive; do not assume an exact storage layout across interpreters.

title: A self-import accesses a module before its required names are initialized

where.summary: A module imports itself or accesses itself through an import during initialization.
preconditions: The import path requests a name that has not yet been defined.
where.location_template: At {location} in {target}, inspect: A module imports itself or accesses itself through an import during initialization.

how.mechanism: Import cycles can expose the partially initialized module object before the required definitions exist.
how.trigger_template: Import {module} in a fresh isolated interpreter and reach {premature_name_access}.

what.observable_failure: Import resolution or attribute access fails before module initialization completes.
what.oracle_template: Under {module_contract}, assert successful initialization and availability of the required names at their actual use sites.

applicability_notes: A self-import can succeed by returning the cached partial module; it does not unconditionally raise ImportError.

title: A sequence index lacks the required integer or slice protocol

where.summary: A built-in sequence is indexed with an unsupported index value.
preconditions: The value is neither a slice nor an object accepted by the integer-index protocol.
where.location_template: At {location} in {target}, inspect: A built-in sequence is indexed with an unsupported index value.

how.mechanism: Sequence subscription validates its index protocol rather than interpreting arbitrary strings or floats as indices.
how.trigger_template: Apply {index_value} to {sequence}, including an invalid-type case and a valid integer-index control.

what.observable_failure: Subscription raises TypeError instead of the required element or invalid-input handling.
what.oracle_template: Under {index_contract}, assert the supported index domain and the required rejection policy.

applicability_notes: Objects implementing __index__ can be valid without being int instances; mapping keys and custom __getitem__ have different rules.
